verdict.rationale: Honeybadger's docs say it automatically groups identical or similar errors into one fault while keeping each occurrence navigable. Grouping can be customized per exception by changing the error class, component, or stack trace, or by sending a custom fingerprint. A community user independently praises the deduping. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the default grouping rules (stack-trace fingerprinting is only implied), and evidence of UI-side merge/split or retroactive regrouping when grouping goes wrong.

support.subject: As a developer, the platform groups thousands of duplicate events into one issue via stack-trace fingerprinting, and I can customize the grouping when it gets it wrong
